meta.title: Two Clock Domains
meta.subtitle: Every ghost on a client lives in the server's past or the client's future — and ownership picks which

views.label: Ownership is the selector
views.note: One prefab, one dropdown, and the same entity lands in different time domains on different machines.

views.label: The past: a delay line
views.note: Snapshots go into a ring; the read pointer trails the write pointer by a fixed delay. Late, never wrong.

views.label: The future: speculative execution
views.note: Restore to the last confirmed tick, resimulate to now, every frame. Fast, often wrong, always corrected.

views.label: The contagion rule
views.note: Two entities in different time domains cannot interact correctly. Contact spreads prediction.

boundaries.label: the server's past · a delay line · late, never wrong
the client's future · speculative execution · fast, often wrong

cards.title: Two domains, one sentence each
items: Interpolated: the entity lives in the server's past, played back from a buffer
Predicted: the entity lives in the client's future, resimulated every frame
OwnerPredicted: the owning client predicts it, every other client interpolates it
So one prefab sits in different time domains on different machines

cards.title: The contagion rule
items: A predicted entity cannot correctly interact with an interpolated one
They are not simulating the same instant — one is ahead, one is behind
Anything a predicted entity touches must itself be predicted
This is why predicting one thing quietly ends up predicting a whole subsystem

cards.title: What each mode costs per frame
items: Interpolated: two buffer reads and a lerp, no gameplay systems run
Predicted: ticks_behind × predicted entities × your predicted systems
OwnerPredicted: one entity pays the replay bill, N−1 pay almost nothing
The replay count is the same for every predicted ghost, so the set size is the knob
